openai.name: OpenAI
openai.blurb: Maker of ChatGPT and the GPT model family; largest consumer AI product and a top-two API vendor. Building its own datacenter capacity (Stargate) with Oracle, SoftBank and others.
openai.overview: OpenAI builds and sells frontier models. Revenue comes from ChatGPT subscriptions (consumer, Plus/Pro, Team and Enterprise seats), API usage billed per token, and a growing ads and commerce layer inside ChatGPT. It was restructured in 2025 into a public-benefit corporation controlled by the non-profit, with Microsoft holding roughly 27%. The business is capital-intensive: it has committed hundreds of billions to compute through Stargate (Oracle, SoftBank, Crusoe), AMD and NVIDIA, so its economics depend on sustaining consumer scale and enterprise pricing power long enough to pay for that capacity.

anthropic.name: Anthropic
anthropic.blurb: Safety-focused lab behind Claude; strongest position in coding and enterprise API usage. Backed by Amazon and Google; trains on AWS Trainium and Google TPUs as well as NVIDIA.
anthropic.overview: Anthropic trains the Claude model family and sells it almost entirely to businesses and developers: API usage via its own platform plus Amazon Bedrock and Google Vertex, Claude Code for software teams, and enterprise seat plans. Coding and agentic workloads are its strongest segment, which is why it is the most exposed lab to developer-tool demand. It is backed by Amazon and Google, trains across NVIDIA GPUs, AWS Trainium and Google TPUs, and positions itself on safety research and interpretability. Context: an IPO was filed in 2026, making it the first frontier lab to test public markets.

google.name: Google / Alphabet
google.blurb: Full-stack: Gemini models from DeepMind, TPUs designed with Broadcom, Google Cloud distribution, Android and Search defaults, plus Waymo and Isomorphic Labs as Alphabet bets.
google.overview: Alphabet is the only company that owns every layer of the stack: Gemini models from DeepMind, TPU silicon co-designed with Broadcom, Google Cloud as the distribution channel, and Search, Android, Chrome and Workspace as surfaces with billions of users. The core business model is still advertising, so the strategic question is whether AI answers cannibalise or extend search revenue. Google Cloud is the fastest-growing segment, and Alphabet also funds Waymo and Isomorphic Labs as long-dated bets.

meta.name: Meta
meta.blurb: Open-weight Llama models, Meta AI across 3B users, and the 2025 Superintelligence Labs reset funded by a 49% stake in Scale AI. Builds MTIA silicon with Broadcom and gigawatt datacenters.
meta.overview: Meta monetises AI indirectly: better ranking and ad targeting across Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, and Meta AI as a free assistant reaching billions of users. It open-sources Llama to commoditise the model layer rather than selling API access. In 2025 it reset its research effort as Meta Superintelligence Labs, bought 49% of Scale AI and hired aggressively, while committing to gigawatt-scale datacenters and MTIA custom chips with Broadcom. It is the largest AI spender with no cloud business to sell the capacity.

xai.name: xAI
xai.blurb: Elon Musk's lab; Grok models distributed through X and Tesla, trained on the Colossus cluster in Memphis, the largest single-site GPU build. Merged with X in 2025.
xai.overview: xAI trains the Grok models and distributes them through X (formerly Twitter), the Grok app, Tesla vehicles and an API. After merging with X in 2025 the combined company monetises through X Premium subscriptions, advertising and enterprise API deals. Its edge is compute: the Colossus cluster in Memphis is the largest single-site GPU build, funded by multi-billion equity and debt rounds from SoftBank, Gulf sovereign funds, a16z and Sequoia. It is the most capital-hungry lab relative to revenue.

mistral.name: Mistral AI
mistral.blurb: Europe's flagship lab; open-weight and enterprise models, sovereign-AI positioning, ASML as anchor investor in 2025.
mistral.overview: Mistral is Europe's leading lab, selling open-weight and proprietary models to enterprises and governments that want data sovereignty. Revenue comes from API usage, on-premise deployments, Le Chat subscriptions and large public-sector and defence contracts in France and the EU. ASML became its anchor investor in 2025, and it is building its own datacenter capacity near Paris. Its pitch is a credible alternative to US labs for regulated European industries.

cohere.name: Cohere
cohere.blurb: Enterprise-only models (Command, Embed, Rerank) with private deployment; Canadian sovereign compute partner.
cohere.overview: Cohere sells language models exclusively to enterprises and governments, with a focus on private deployment inside a customer's own cloud or on-premise. Its Command, Embed and Rerank models power retrieval and agent workflows in banks, telcos and public bodies, and it is Canada's sovereign-AI partner. It avoids the consumer market entirely and competes on security, data control and cost rather than frontier benchmarks.

deepseek.name: DeepSeek
deepseek.blurb: High-Flyer-backed lab whose R1 reasoning model (Jan 2025) reset cost expectations; open weights, very low API prices, constrained by export controls.
deepseek.overview: DeepSeek is a research lab funded by the Chinese quant fund High-Flyer. Its R1 reasoning model in January 2025 showed frontier-class results at a fraction of the assumed training cost, which reset investor expectations for compute spend. It releases open weights and runs a very low-priced API, so revenue is small; the lab matters for its influence on pricing and on China's domestic ecosystem. US export controls on advanced chips constrain how fast it can scale.

alibaba.name: Alibaba (Qwen / Alibaba Cloud)
alibaba.blurb: Qwen is the most-downloaded open-weight model family; Alibaba Cloud is China's largest AI cloud and supplies Apple Intelligence in China.
alibaba.overview: Alibaba is China's largest cloud provider and the home of Qwen, the most-downloaded open-weight model family worldwide. Alibaba Cloud sells compute, model hosting and enterprise AI services, and supplies the models behind Apple Intelligence in China. The core business remains e-commerce (Taobao, Tmall), but management has committed over $50B to AI infrastructure, making Alibaba Cloud the main domestic alternative to US hyperscalers for Chinese enterprises.

amazon.name: Amazon / AWS
amazon.blurb: Largest cloud, Trainium custom chips, Bedrock model marketplace, $8B Anthropic investment and Project Rainier training clusters; Nova in-house models.
amazon.overview: AWS is the largest cloud and the main way Amazon monetises AI: renting GPUs and its own Trainium chips, selling third-party models through Bedrock, and bundling AI into databases and developer tools. Amazon invested $8B in Anthropic and built the Project Rainier Trainium clusters for it, making Anthropic both a customer and a showcase for custom silicon. Retail and advertising benefit from AI in logistics, search and ads. AWS is Amazon's main profit engine, so AI capex is funded from cloud margins.

microsoft.name: Microsoft
microsoft.blurb: Azure is OpenAI's primary cloud and holds a ~27% stake after the 2025 restructuring; Copilot across Office, GitHub and Windows; MAI in-house models; Nuance DAX in healthcare.
microsoft.overview: Microsoft monetises AI through Azure (renting compute and hosting OpenAI and other models), Copilot seats in Microsoft 365, GitHub Copilot, and Windows. Azure is OpenAI's primary cloud, and after the 2025 restructuring Microsoft holds about 27% of OpenAI plus IP rights to its models. It is also building its own MAI models and Maia chips to reduce dependence. Enterprise distribution is its edge: it can attach AI to software that companies already pay for.

ai21.name: AI21 Labs
ai21.blurb: Jamba hybrid SSM-transformer models for enterprise; NVIDIA and Google investors.
ai21.overview: AI21 Labs is an Israeli lab that sells enterprise language models and agent tooling, notably the Jamba family that mixes state-space and transformer layers for long-context efficiency. It licenses models to enterprises and through cloud marketplaces, and counts NVIDIA and Google among investors. It is a smaller player that competes on specialised architectures and private deployment rather than scale.

moonshot.name: Moonshot AI
moonshot.blurb: Kimi models; K2 (2025) was a leading open-weight agentic model. Alibaba-backed.
moonshot.overview: Moonshot AI is a Beijing lab behind the Kimi assistant and models. Its K2 model in 2025 was among the strongest open-weight agentic models, raising its profile outside China. Revenue comes from the consumer Kimi app and API access; Alibaba is a major backer. Like other Chinese labs it competes mainly on open weights, low prices and long context.

zhipu.name: Zhipu AI (Z.ai)
zhipu.blurb: Tsinghua spin-out behind GLM models; state-backed, IPO track in Hong Kong.
zhipu.overview: Zhipu AI (Z.ai) is a Tsinghua University spin-out that builds the GLM model family and sells enterprise and government AI deployments across China. It is heavily state- and SOE-backed and was among the first Chinese labs to pursue an IPO in Hong Kong. Its business is a mix of API revenue, on-premise projects and consumer apps; it is on the US entity list.

nvidia.name: NVIDIA
nvidia.blurb: Owns the AI training and inference accelerator market with Blackwell and Rubin, plus NVLink/InfiniBand networking and the CUDA moat. Also the most active strategic investor in AI startups and neoclouds.
nvidia.overview: NVIDIA sells the accelerators, networking and systems that nearly all AI training and most inference run on. Revenue is overwhelmingly datacenter: GPUs (Blackwell, Rubin), NVLink and InfiniBand/Ethernet networking, and full rack-scale systems sold to hyperscalers, neoclouds, labs and sovereigns. The CUDA software ecosystem is the moat that keeps customers from switching to AMD or custom chips. It is also the most active strategic investor in AI, taking stakes in OpenAI, Anthropic, CoreWeave, xAI and dozens of startups, which critics call circular financing.

amd.name: AMD
amd.blurb: Instinct MI300/MI350/MI450 GPUs; landed OpenAI as anchor customer (6 GW deal, 2025) and supplies Oracle and Microsoft; ROCm software is the gap to close.
amd.overview: AMD is the main merchant alternative to NVIDIA for AI GPUs, selling the Instinct MI300/MI350/MI450 line to hyperscalers and labs, alongside its CPU business (EPYC server chips, Ryzen PCs) that funds the effort. In 2025 it signed OpenAI as an anchor customer for 6 GW of GPUs, with warrants that could give OpenAI up to 10% of AMD. The gap to close is software: ROCm still lags CUDA in developer adoption.

broadcom.name: Broadcom
broadcom.blurb: Designs custom AI ASICs for Google (TPU), Meta (MTIA), ByteDance and OpenAI, plus Ethernet switching (Tomahawk) for AI clusters.
broadcom.overview: Broadcom is the leading designer of custom AI accelerators (ASICs) for hyperscalers, including Google's TPU, Meta's MTIA, ByteDance's chips and an OpenAI program, plus the Ethernet switch silicon (Tomahawk) that connects AI clusters. It sells design services and chips at high margins and also owns VMware. It is the main beneficiary when cloud providers build their own silicon instead of buying NVIDIA.

intel.name: Intel
intel.blurb: Gaudi accelerators have little share; the strategic question is Intel Foundry (18A, 14A) as a US alternative to TSMC, with US government and NVIDIA stakes taken in 2025.
intel.overview: Intel is the former CPU leader trying to become the US alternative to TSMC. Its Gaudi AI accelerators have little share; the strategic asset is Intel Foundry and its 18A and 14A process nodes. In 2025 the US government took a roughly 10% stake and NVIDIA invested $5B, tying Intel's future to national-security industrial policy. Revenue still comes mostly from PC and server CPUs.

marvell.name: Marvell
marvell.blurb: Custom silicon partner for Amazon Trainium and Microsoft Maia; optical interconnect and DSPs for AI datacenters.
marvell.overview: Marvell designs custom silicon and interconnect for datacenters. It is the design partner for Amazon's Trainium and Microsoft's Maia accelerators and sells optical DSPs and electro-optics that link GPUs across racks. Its model is design-services plus chip sales to a few hyperscaler customers, so revenue is concentrated but tied directly to AI capex.

cerebras.name: Cerebras
cerebras.blurb: Wafer-scale chips for fast inference; G42 is its anchor customer; IPO track.
cerebras.overview: Cerebras builds wafer-scale processors, a single chip the size of a dinner plate, aimed at very fast inference and training. It sells systems and, increasingly, cloud inference by the token. G42 of Abu Dhabi is its anchor customer and investor, which delayed its IPO over national-security review. It is one of the few hardware startups with meaningful revenue.

groq.name: Groq
groq.blurb: LPU inference chips with SRAM-heavy design; GroqCloud; Saudi datacenter deal with Aramco.
groq.overview: Groq makes LPU inference chips that use on-chip SRAM instead of HBM to deliver very low latency, and sells access mainly through GroqCloud by the token. It signed a large datacenter deal in Saudi Arabia with Aramco Digital and raised at a multi-billion valuation. The bet is that inference economics will favour specialised chips over general GPUs.

qualcomm.name: Qualcomm
qualcomm.blurb: On-device NPUs in Snapdragon phones and PCs; entering datacenter inference with AI200/AI250 (2025).
qualcomm.overview: Qualcomm dominates smartphone processors and modems, and its Snapdragon NPUs run on-device AI in Android phones and Windows PCs. It licenses patents (QTL) and sells chips (QCT). In 2025 it entered datacenter inference with the AI200/AI250 rack systems, with Humain in Saudi Arabia as first customer. Its edge AI position is strong; datacenter is unproven.

huawei.name: Huawei
huawei.blurb: Ascend 910C/950 accelerators and CloudMatrix systems are China's domestic NVIDIA alternative, fabbed at SMIC under sanctions.
huawei.overview: Huawei is China's domestic answer to NVIDIA: its Ascend 910C and 950 accelerators and CloudMatrix systems are the main option for Chinese labs cut off from advanced US chips. It is privately held, fabs at SMIC under sanctions, and also sells telecom equipment, phones and Huawei Cloud. Its chip output is capped by domestic fab capacity rather than demand.

sambanova.name: SambaNova
sambanova.blurb: Reconfigurable dataflow chips for inference; pivoted to cloud inference; Intel acquisition talks in 2025.
sambanova.overview: SambaNova builds reconfigurable dataflow processors for AI inference and sells them as systems and through its own cloud. It targets enterprises and sovereign customers that want on-premise alternatives to NVIDIA. After slower-than-hoped sales it pivoted to cloud inference and explored a sale to Intel in 2025.

tsmc.name: TSMC
tsmc.blurb: Fabs essentially every leading AI accelerator (NVIDIA, AMD, Broadcom, Google TPU, Trainium, Apple); CoWoS packaging is the binding constraint on GPU supply. Building in Arizona.
tsmc.overview: TSMC is the contract chipmaker that fabricates essentially every leading AI accelerator: NVIDIA, AMD, Broadcom's custom ASICs, Google TPUs, Amazon Trainium and Apple silicon. It sells wafers and advanced packaging (CoWoS), and CoWoS capacity has been the binding constraint on GPU supply. It is building fabs in Arizona under US pressure, but leading-edge production stays in Taiwan, which makes it the central geopolitical risk in AI supply.

asml.name: ASML
asml.blurb: Sole supplier of EUV lithography; High-NA EUV ramping for 2nm-class nodes. Took a €1.3B stake in Mistral in 2025.
asml.overview: ASML is the only maker of extreme-ultraviolet lithography machines, the tools required to manufacture chips at 7nm and below. Every advanced fab (TSMC, Samsung, Intel, SK hynix) buys from it, and High-NA EUV is ramping for 2nm-class nodes. Export controls bar sales of EUV to China. In 2025 it took a €1.3B stake in Mistral, a rare move down the stack.

skhynix.name: SK hynix
skhynix.blurb: Leading HBM supplier (HBM3E, HBM4) to NVIDIA; HBM is the gating component for every accelerator generation.
skhynix.overview: SK hynix is the leading supplier of high-bandwidth memory (HBM), the stacked DRAM packaged next to AI accelerators. It is NVIDIA's primary HBM3E and HBM4 source and HBM is sold out through 2026, which has lifted its margins to records. It also makes conventional DRAM and NAND; memory pricing cycles remain the main risk.

micron.name: Micron
micron.blurb: US HBM supplier gaining share at NVIDIA and AMD; memory pricing is the swing factor in its AI exposure.
micron.overview: Micron is the US memory maker and the number-two or three HBM supplier, gaining share at NVIDIA and AMD. It sells DRAM, NAND and HBM to datacenter, PC and mobile customers. AI demand has pulled HBM and server DRAM into shortage, and Micron is expanding fabs in Idaho and New York with CHIPS Act support.

samsung.name: Samsung Electronics
samsung.blurb: HBM number three and second-source foundry (Tesla AI6 contract, 2025); Galaxy phones ship Gemini on-device.
samsung.overview: Samsung Electronics is the world's largest memory maker and second-largest foundry. In AI it supplies HBM (behind SK hynix), DRAM, and foundry capacity, and in 2025 won Tesla's AI6 chip contract for its Texas fab. Its Galaxy phones ship Gemini on-device. The business spans phones, displays and appliances, but memory drives profits, and AI-driven HBM demand pushed its market cap past $1T.

oracle.name: Oracle
oracle.blurb: Turned OCI into an AI cloud by building Stargate datacenters for OpenAI ($300B contract) and hosting xAI, Meta and TikTok; Oracle Health in clinical AI.
oracle.overview: Oracle turned its lagging cloud (OCI) into an AI infrastructure business by building and leasing giant datacenters to OpenAI (a $300B multi-year contract), xAI, Meta and TikTok. It finances the builds with heavy debt and partners like Crusoe. Legacy revenue comes from databases and applications, and Oracle Health (formerly Cerner) is its route into clinical AI. The stock trades on remaining performance obligations rather than current earnings.

coreweave.name: CoreWeave
coreweave.blurb: Largest GPU neocloud; IPO March 2025; Microsoft and OpenAI are anchor customers; NVIDIA investor and supplier. Growth financed with GPU-backed debt.
coreweave.overview: CoreWeave is the largest GPU-only cloud (neocloud): it buys NVIDIA systems, finances them with GPU-backed debt, and rents the capacity under multi-year contracts to Microsoft, OpenAI, Meta and labs. It went public in March 2025. NVIDIA is both supplier and investor and has agreed to buy unsold capacity. The model is high growth with high leverage and customer concentration.

databricks.name: Databricks
databricks.blurb: Lakehouse plus Mosaic AI; the enterprise data platform where fine-tuning and agent building happen; deep Anthropic and OpenAI partnerships.
databricks.overview: Databricks sells a data and AI platform (the lakehouse) where enterprises store data, train and fine-tune models, and build agents. It charges by consumption and has become one of the largest private software companies, with deep partnerships with Anthropic and OpenAI to serve their models on customer data. It competes with Snowflake and the hyperscalers' own data services.

snowflake.name: Snowflake
snowflake.blurb: Data cloud adding Cortex AI and agents; competes with Databricks for the enterprise data layer.
snowflake.overview: Snowflake is a cloud data warehouse that charges by compute consumption. It is adding Cortex AI, hosted models and agents so that customers can run AI on data already inside Snowflake. Its main competition is Databricks for the enterprise data layer; its risk is that AI workloads pull data toward lakehouse formats.

nebius.name: Nebius
nebius.blurb: Ex-Yandex AI cloud; $17B Microsoft capacity contract (2025); building in Finland, Paris, New Jersey.
nebius.overview: Nebius is the AI cloud spun out of Yandex's non-Russian assets and listed on Nasdaq. It builds and operates GPU datacenters in Finland, France and the US and rents capacity; a $17B multi-year contract with Microsoft in 2025 anchored its growth. It also holds stakes in Toloka, ClickHouse and Avride.

lambda.name: Lambda
lambda.blurb: GPU cloud for developers and labs; Microsoft multi-billion capacity deal (2025); IPO track.
lambda.overview: Lambda is a GPU cloud for developers and labs that started as a workstation seller. It rents NVIDIA capacity on demand and under reserved contracts, signed a multi-billion deal with Microsoft in 2025, and is preparing an IPO. It competes with CoreWeave and Nebius on price and developer experience.

crusoe.name: Crusoe
crusoe.blurb: Energy-first datacenter developer; builds the Abilene, Texas Stargate campus for Oracle/OpenAI; gas and stranded-energy power.
crusoe.overview: Crusoe develops and operates AI datacenters where power is cheapest, originally using flared natural gas and now large gas and renewable campuses. It is the builder of the Abilene, Texas Stargate campus for Oracle and OpenAI and also runs its own GPU cloud. Its model is energy-first real estate plus compute leasing.

scale.name: Scale AI
scale.blurb: Data labelling and evaluation for labs; Meta bought 49% for $14.3B in 2025 and hired CEO Alexandr Wang, pushing OpenAI and Google to competitors like Surge and Mercor.
scale.overview: Scale AI supplies the human-labelled and expert data used to train and evaluate frontier models, plus evaluation tooling for governments. In 2025 Meta bought 49% for $14.3B and hired its CEO, which led OpenAI and Google to shift spend to rivals such as Surge and Mercor. It now operates as a Meta-aligned data provider with a shrinking neutral-vendor role.

togetherai.name: Together AI
togetherai.blurb: Open-model inference and fine-tuning cloud; research on efficient attention (FlashAttention).
togetherai.overview: Together AI runs a cloud for open-weight models: inference by the token, fine-tuning and dedicated GPU clusters. It also publishes research on efficient training (its team co-created FlashAttention). It competes with Fireworks, Baseten and the hyperscalers to be the default place to run open models.

fireworks.name: Fireworks AI
fireworks.blurb: Fast inference platform for open models; ex-PyTorch team.
fireworks.overview: Fireworks AI is an inference platform founded by former PyTorch leads. It serves open and custom models with low latency and sells by the token or dedicated deployment, with customers in coding tools and consumer apps. It competes with Together AI and Baseten on speed and price.

huggingface.name: Hugging Face
huggingface.blurb: The GitHub of models: hub for open weights and datasets, Transformers library, LeRobot for robotics; monetises enterprise hub and inference.
huggingface.overview: Hugging Face is the hub where open models and datasets are published, with its Transformers library the standard toolkit. It monetises through enterprise hub subscriptions, hosted inference and compute partnerships, and is expanding into robotics with LeRobot. It is the neutral distribution layer for open-weight AI.

baseten.name: Baseten
baseten.blurb: Inference infrastructure for production models; multi-cloud capacity.
baseten.overview: Baseten provides inference infrastructure for companies running models in production, abstracting GPUs across multiple clouds with autoscaling and performance tooling. It charges for compute usage and counts fast-growing AI startups among customers; it competes with Fireworks, Together and Modal.

vast.name: VAST Data
vast.blurb: AI storage and data platform used by CoreWeave, xAI and sovereign clouds.
vast.overview: VAST Data sells storage and data infrastructure built for AI clusters, used by CoreWeave, xAI and sovereign clouds to feed GPUs at scale. It licenses software that runs on commodity hardware and has expanded into a broader data platform with database and agent features.

salesforce.name: Salesforce
salesforce.blurb: Agentforce is the incumbent-CRM bet on agents; Data Cloud and Informatica acquisition for the data layer.
salesforce.overview: Salesforce is the largest CRM vendor and sells software by subscription seat. Agentforce is its bet on charging for AI agents by conversation or outcome rather than per user, and Data Cloud plus the Informatica acquisition supply the data layer. The risk is that agents reduce the seat counts its core model depends on.

servicenow.name: ServiceNow
servicenow.blurb: Now Assist and AI agents across IT, HR and customer workflows; acquired Moveworks for $2.85B.
servicenow.overview: ServiceNow sells workflow software for IT, HR and customer service by subscription. It embeds Now Assist and AI agents into those workflows and acquired Moveworks for $2.85B to add an employee-facing assistant. It is one of the clearest cases of an incumbent charging a premium tier for AI features.

palantir.name: Palantir
palantir.blurb: AIP platform drove the fastest growth among large software companies; government and now commercial agents on an ontology layer.
palantir.overview: Palantir sells data-integration and decision software to governments and enterprises. Its AIP platform, which lets customers run models over an ontology of their operations, drove the fastest growth of any large software company in 2024-25, especially in US commercial and defence. Pricing is large contracts rather than seats, and the stock carries an exceptionally high multiple.

adobe.name: Adobe
adobe.blurb: Firefly generative models inside Creative Cloud; defends against Midjourney, Runway and Canva.
adobe.overview: Adobe sells creative, document and marketing software by subscription. Its Firefly models generate images and video inside Photoshop, Premiere and Express, trained on licensed content so enterprises can use them safely. It defends its franchise against Midjourney, Runway, Canva and OpenAI's image tools.

sap.name: SAP
sap.blurb: Joule copilot and agents across ERP; sovereign-cloud positioning in Europe.
sap.overview: SAP is the largest enterprise resource planning vendor. It is embedding the Joule copilot and agents across finance, supply-chain and HR software and uses its cloud migration programme to upsell AI. It positions itself as the sovereign-cloud option for European industry.

cursor.name: Cursor (Anysphere)
cursor.blurb: AI code editor that reached $500M+ ARR in under two years; builds on Anthropic, OpenAI and its own models.
cursor.overview: Cursor is an AI-native code editor from Anysphere. It charges developers and teams monthly subscriptions plus usage, routes requests to Anthropic, OpenAI and its own models, and reached over $500M in annual recurring revenue within two years, the fastest software ramp on record. Its margin depends on model costs it does not control.

uipath.name: UiPath
uipath.blurb: RPA incumbent repositioning as an agentic automation platform.
uipath.overview: UiPath is the leading robotic process automation vendor, selling software that automates repetitive back-office tasks. It is repositioning as an agentic automation platform that orchestrates AI agents alongside its bots. Growth has slowed and it competes with Microsoft and startups offering agents directly.

cognition.name: Cognition
cognition.blurb: Devin autonomous coding agent; acquired Windsurf after Google's $2.4B licensing-and-hire deal for its founders.
cognition.overview: Cognition builds Devin, an autonomous software-engineering agent sold to enterprises and developers. In 2025 it acquired Windsurf (the AI editor) after Google paid $2.4B to license its technology and hire its founders, giving Cognition a product line from assistant to full agent.

replit.name: Replit
replit.blurb: Agent-first app builder; ARR grew ~10x in 2025 on 'vibe coding' demand.
replit.overview: Replit is a browser-based development platform whose Agent builds and deploys applications from prompts. Subscriptions and usage from non-professional builders drove roughly tenfold revenue growth in 2025. It competes with Lovable, Bolt and Cursor in the 'vibe coding' segment.

glean.name: Glean
glean.blurb: Enterprise search and agent platform over company data.
glean.overview: Glean sells enterprise search and an agent platform that connects to a company's internal apps and documents with permissions preserved. It charges per seat and is used by large tech and financial firms. It competes with Microsoft Copilot and ChatGPT Enterprise for the internal-knowledge use case.

harvey.name: Harvey
harvey.blurb: Legal AI for law firms and in-house teams; OpenAI-backed, multi-model since 2025.
harvey.overview: Harvey builds AI for lawyers: research, drafting and workflow tools sold to large law firms and corporate legal teams by seat. It started on OpenAI models and became multi-model in 2025. It is the best-funded vertical legal AI company and competes with Thomson Reuters and LexisNexis.

sierra.name: Sierra
sierra.blurb: Customer-service agents from Bret Taylor; outcome-based pricing.
sierra.overview: Sierra, founded by Bret Taylor and Clay Bavor, builds customer-service agents for consumer brands and prices on outcomes such as resolved conversations rather than seats. It competes with Decagon and incumbents like Salesforce and Zendesk.

lovable.name: Lovable
lovable.overview: Lovable is a Stockholm startup whose product turns prompts into working web apps. Subscription revenue grew to over $100M in annual run-rate within a year, making it Europe's fastest-growing startup. It targets non-developers and competes with Replit and Bolt.

writer.name: Writer
writer.blurb: Enterprise generative AI platform with its own Palmyra models.
writer.overview: Writer sells a generative AI platform to enterprises with its own Palmyra models, emphasising governance, brand control and on-premise options. It charges by seat and usage and competes with OpenAI and Anthropic enterprise offerings.

c3ai.name: C3.ai
c3ai.blurb: Enterprise AI applications for industrials and government; founder transition in 2025.
c3ai.overview: C3.ai sells pre-built enterprise AI applications for industrials, energy, defence and government, often through partners like Baker Hughes and Microsoft. Revenue is subscription and pilot-based; growth has been uneven and founder Tom Siebel stepped back as CEO in 2025.

decagon.name: Decagon
decagon.blurb: Customer-support agents competing with Sierra; a16z and Accel backed.
decagon.overview: Decagon builds AI customer-support agents for companies such as Duolingo and Notion, priced per conversation. It competes directly with Sierra and raised large rounds from a16z and Accel in 2025.

waymo.name: Waymo
waymo.blurb: Alphabet's robotaxi unit; the only scaled driverless service in the US, expanding to a dozen metros plus Tokyo and London; Zeekr and Hyundai vehicle platforms.
waymo.overview: Waymo is Alphabet's autonomous-driving unit and the only driverless ride-hailing service operating at scale in the US, with hundreds of thousands of paid rides a week across Phoenix, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Austin and more. It earns fares and partners with Uber in some cities; vehicles come from Jaguar, Zeekr and Hyundai. It is loss-making and funded by Alphabet plus outside rounds.

tesla.name: Tesla
tesla.blurb: Vision-only FSD, Austin robotaxi pilot (2025), Cybercab, Optimus humanoid and in-house AI5/AI6 chips fabbed at Samsung and TSMC; the valuation is a bet on autonomy.
tesla.overview: Tesla is an electric-vehicle and energy-storage company whose valuation rests on autonomy: vision-only FSD sold as a subscription, a robotaxi service piloted in Austin in 2025, the purpose-built Cybercab, and the Optimus humanoid. It designs its own AI5/AI6 chips, fabbed at Samsung and TSMC, and trains on its Cortex cluster. Cars still generate most revenue.

baidu.name: Baidu Apollo
baidu.blurb: Apollo Go runs the largest robotaxi fleet in China (Wuhan, Beijing), expanding to the Middle East and Europe with Uber and Lyft.
baidu.overview: Baidu is China's search company and its Apollo Go unit runs the largest robotaxi fleet in China, with fully driverless service in Wuhan and Beijing. It earns fares and is expanding to the Middle East and Europe with Uber and Lyft. Baidu also sells ERNIE models and Kunlun chips through its cloud.

mobileye.name: Mobileye
mobileye.blurb: ADAS incumbent (EyeQ) moving to eyes-off systems; VW ID.Buzz robotaxi platform with Uber and Lyft.
mobileye.overview: Mobileye, majority-owned by Intel, supplies the EyeQ chips and software behind most driver-assistance systems. It sells to carmakers per vehicle and is moving up to eyes-off and robotaxi systems, including the VW ID.Buzz platform deployed with Uber and Lyft. Its challenge is automakers insourcing software.

bostondynamics.name: Boston Dynamics
bostondynamics.blurb: Hyundai-owned; Spot and Stretch in production, electric Atlas humanoid heading to Hyundai factories; Google DeepMind partnership on Atlas intelligence.
bostondynamics.overview: Boston Dynamics, owned by Hyundai, sells the Spot quadruped and Stretch warehouse robot and is industrialising the electric Atlas humanoid for Hyundai's factories. Revenue is hardware sales and service contracts; Google DeepMind supplies learning models for Atlas. It is the most recognised robotics brand but still small in revenue.

unitree.name: Unitree
unitree.blurb: Volume leader in quadrupeds and low-cost humanoids (G1 from ~$16k); Shanghai IPO filed 2025.
unitree.overview: Unitree is the volume leader in legged robots, selling quadrupeds and humanoids (G1 from about $16,000) to researchers, universities and early commercial users. Low prices from Chinese supply chains made it the default research platform. It filed for a Shanghai IPO in 2025.

ponyai.name: Pony.ai
ponyai.blurb: Robotaxi operator in four Chinese tier-1 cities, Gen-7 vehicles with Toyota and GAC; Nasdaq and Hong Kong listed.
ponyai.overview: Pony.ai operates robotaxis in Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou and Shenzhen with its seventh-generation vehicles built with Toyota and GAC. It earns fares and licenses its driver, and is listed on Nasdaq and in Hong Kong. Unit economics improve as it removes safety operators.

weride.name: WeRide
weride.blurb: Robotaxis, robobuses and sweepers; Uber partnership across Abu Dhabi, Dubai and Europe; Nasdaq and Hong Kong listed.
weride.overview: WeRide runs robotaxis, robobuses and autonomous sweepers, with a broad Uber partnership covering Abu Dhabi, Dubai and parts of Europe. It is dual-listed on Nasdaq and in Hong Kong and earns from fares, vehicle sales and services.

zoox.name: Zoox
zoox.blurb: Amazon-owned purpose-built robotaxi; launched public rides in Las Vegas (2025), San Francisco next.
zoox.overview: Zoox is Amazon's robotaxi company, building a purpose-designed bidirectional vehicle with no steering wheel. It launched public rides in Las Vegas in 2025 with San Francisco next. It is fully funded by Amazon and does not yet contribute revenue.

aurora.name: Aurora Innovation
aurora.blurb: First driverless commercial trucking lane (Dallas-Houston, 2025); Volvo and PACCAR platforms, NVIDIA Thor compute.
aurora.overview: Aurora Innovation develops the Aurora Driver for heavy trucks and launched the first driverless commercial freight lane between Dallas and Houston in 2025. It earns per-mile fees from shippers and plans to sell the driver to Volvo and PACCAR trucks using NVIDIA Thor compute.

figure.name: Figure AI
figure.blurb: Humanoid startup with Helix VLA model; BMW pilot; raised $1B+ in 2025 from Parkway, NVIDIA, Intel Capital, Brookfield.
figure.overview: Figure AI builds general-purpose humanoid robots and the Helix vision-language-action model that controls them. It runs a BMW pilot and targets manufacturing and logistics before homes, with hardware sold or leased. It raised over $1B in 2025 at a $39B valuation from Parkway, NVIDIA, Intel Capital and Brookfield.

agibot.name: AgiBot
agibot.blurb: Shipped thousands of humanoids in 2025; backdoor listing in Shanghai; state-backed Chinese champion.
agibot.overview: AgiBot is a Shanghai humanoid maker that shipped thousands of units in 2025, more than any Western rival, backed by state funds and listed via a reverse takeover in Shanghai. It sells robots for research, retail and factory pilots and benefits from China's industrial-policy push into embodied AI.

agility.name: Agility Robotics
agility.blurb: Digit bipedal robot deployed at GXO and Schaeffler; robots-as-a-service model.
agility.overview: Agility Robotics makes Digit, a bipedal robot that moves totes in warehouses for GXO and Schaeffler. It sells robots-as-a-service, charging per hour or per task, and builds them at its RoboFab plant in Oregon. It is the most commercially deployed humanoid in logistics.

nuro.name: Nuro
nuro.blurb: Pivoted from delivery pods to licensing its driver; Uber and Lucid robotaxi program with Uber investment.
nuro.overview: Nuro built delivery robots and pivoted in 2024 to licensing its autonomous driver. Its main programme is a robotaxi with Lucid vehicles and Uber as operator and investor. Revenue comes from licensing and development fees.

apptronik.name: Apptronik
apptronik.blurb: Apollo humanoid; Google DeepMind partnership and investment; Mercedes and GXO pilots; Jabil manufacturing.
apptronik.overview: Apptronik builds the Apollo humanoid for logistics and manufacturing, with pilots at Mercedes-Benz and GXO and manufacturing by Jabil. Google DeepMind is both investor and AI partner. It sells and leases robots to industrial customers.

1x.name: 1X Technologies
1x.blurb: NEO home humanoid, pre-orders opened 2025 at $20k; OpenAI-backed; teleoperation-heavy data strategy.
1x.overview: 1X Technologies builds the NEO humanoid for the home and opened pre-orders at about $20,000 (or a monthly subscription) in 2025. Early units rely heavily on teleoperation to collect training data. It is backed by OpenAI, EQT and Tiger and competes with Figure and Tesla Optimus.

kodiak.name: Kodiak AI
kodiak.blurb: Driverless trucks in the Permian Basin for Atlas Energy; SPAC listing 2025.
kodiak.overview: Kodiak AI runs driverless trucks hauling sand for Atlas Energy in the Permian Basin and develops long-haul autonomy. It listed via SPAC in 2025 and earns per-truck service fees. It is smaller than Aurora but earlier to fully driverless commercial operation.

physicalintelligence.name: Physical Intelligence
physicalintelligence.blurb: Robot foundation models (pi0, pi0.5) that run across many robot bodies; backed by Jeff Bezos, OpenAI, Thrive, Lux.
physicalintelligence.overview: Physical Intelligence is a research company building general robot foundation models (pi0, pi0.5) that control many different robot bodies. It does not sell hardware; the plan is to license models to robot makers. It is backed by Jeff Bezos, OpenAI, Thrive and Lux at a multi-billion valuation.

skild.name: Skild AI
skild.blurb: General robot brain trained on simulation at scale; SoftBank, NVIDIA and Samsung investors.
skild.overview: Skild AI trains a general 'robot brain' largely in simulation and licenses it to hardware makers. SoftBank, NVIDIA and Samsung are investors, with a valuation above $10B after 2025 rounds. It competes with Physical Intelligence for the model layer of robotics.

tempus.name: Tempus AI
tempus.blurb: Precision-medicine data and diagnostics; largest clinical-genomic dataset; AI apps for oncology and cardiology.
tempus.overview: Tempus AI sells genomic sequencing and diagnostics to oncologists and licenses its large de-identified clinical and molecular dataset to pharma for drug development. It is listed on Nasdaq; diagnostics drives most revenue while data licensing provides higher margins. It also sells AI applications for cardiology and radiology.

gehealthcare.name: GE HealthCare
gehealthcare.blurb: Most FDA-cleared AI devices of any company; imaging AI embedded in scanners; NVIDIA autonomous-imaging partnership.
gehealthcare.overview: GE HealthCare makes imaging equipment (MRI, CT, ultrasound), patient monitoring and pharmaceutical diagnostics. It holds more FDA-cleared AI devices than any company, embedding AI in scanners to speed scans and flag findings, and is working with NVIDIA on autonomous imaging. Revenue is equipment plus service contracts.

siemenshealthineers.name: Siemens Healthineers
siemenshealthineers.blurb: AI-Rad Companion and scanner-embedded AI; imaging incumbent alongside GE and Philips.
siemenshealthineers.overview: Siemens Healthineers sells imaging and diagnostic equipment and the Varian cancer-therapy business. Its AI-Rad Companion and scanner-embedded AI are sold as software add-ons and subscriptions. It is the European counterpart to GE HealthCare and Philips in imaging AI.

abridge.name: Abridge
abridge.blurb: Leading ambient clinical documentation startup; deep Epic integration; Mayo, Kaiser, Johns Hopkins customers.
abridge.overview: Abridge turns clinician-patient conversations into clinical notes inside the Epic electronic health record. It sells enterprise contracts to health systems such as Mayo, Kaiser and Johns Hopkins and is the leading ambient documentation vendor, competing with Microsoft's Nuance DAX and Ambience.

recursion.name: Recursion
recursion.blurb: TechBio platform merged with Exscientia; NVIDIA-backed BioHive supercomputer; pipeline pruned in 2025 to focus on lead programs.
recursion.overview: Recursion is a TechBio company that runs automated biology experiments and machine learning to find drug candidates, merged with Exscientia in 2024. It is Nasdaq-listed, earns milestone payments from Roche, Sanofi and others, and pruned its pipeline in 2025 to focus capital. NVIDIA backed its BioHive supercomputer.

isomorphic.name: Isomorphic Labs
isomorphic.blurb: Alphabet's drug-discovery company built on AlphaFold 3; Eli Lilly and Novartis partnerships; first external raise $600M (2025).
isomorphic.overview: Isomorphic Labs is Alphabet's drug-discovery company built on AlphaFold 3. It partners with Eli Lilly and Novartis on discovery programmes for milestone and royalty payments and raised $600M externally in 2025. It aims to bring its own designed drugs to the clinic.

openevidence.name: OpenEvidence
openevidence.blurb: Clinical search used by a majority of US physicians; ad-supported; NEJM and JAMA content deals.
openevidence.overview: OpenEvidence is a clinical search and answer engine used by a large share of US physicians. It is free to clinicians and monetises with advertising, with content deals from NEJM and JAMA. It is one of the fastest-adopted tools in medicine and raised at a multi-billion valuation.

hippocratic.name: Hippocratic AI
hippocratic.blurb: Safety-focused patient-facing agents for non-diagnostic tasks (outreach, scheduling, follow-up).
hippocratic.overview: Hippocratic AI builds patient-facing voice agents for non-diagnostic tasks such as appointment reminders, discharge follow-up and chronic-care check-ins, sold to health systems per agent hour. It emphasises safety testing with clinicians and is backed by a16z, General Catalyst and NVIDIA.

ambience.name: Ambience Healthcare
ambience.blurb: Ambient documentation plus coding automation; OpenAI Startup Fund and a16z backed.
ambience.overview: Ambience Healthcare offers ambient clinical documentation plus automated coding and billing support, sold to health systems. It competes with Abridge and Nuance and is backed by the OpenAI Startup Fund, a16z and Kleiner Perkins.

vizai.name: Viz.ai
vizai.blurb: Care-coordination AI starting from stroke detection; first NTAP reimbursement for AI.
vizai.overview: Viz.ai detects conditions such as stroke on scans and coordinates care teams through its app, sold to hospitals by subscription. It won the first Medicare add-on payment for AI software, which set the precedent for reimbursement of clinical AI.

insitro.name: insitro
insitro.blurb: Daphne Koller's ML-driven discovery company; metabolic and neuro programs; Lilly, BMS partnerships.
insitro.overview: insitro, founded by Daphne Koller, uses machine learning on its own cell and patient data to find drug targets in metabolic and neurological disease. It earns from partnerships with Lilly and Bristol Myers Squibb and advances its own pipeline.

generate.name: Generate Biomedicines
generate.blurb: Generative protein design (Chroma); first programs in the clinic; Flagship-founded.
generate.overview: Generate Biomedicines, founded by Flagship Pioneering, uses generative models (Chroma) to design proteins and antibodies. It has programmes in the clinic and partnerships with Amgen and Novartis, earning milestones while building its own pipeline.

insilico.name: Insilico Medicine
insilico.blurb: Rentosertib, the first AI-discovered and AI-designed drug to reach Phase 2 with positive data; Hong Kong IPO.
insilico.overview: Insilico Medicine uses generative AI to find targets and design molecules; its drug rentosertib for lung fibrosis was the first AI-discovered and AI-designed drug to show positive Phase 2 results. It listed in Hong Kong and earns from licensing deals and its Pharma.AI software.

xaira.name: Xaira Therapeutics
xaira.blurb: Launched with $1B from ARCH and Foresite; David Baker's protein-design lineage; Marc Tessier-Lavigne CEO.
xaira.overview: Xaira Therapeutics launched in 2024 with $1B from ARCH and Foresite, built on David Baker's protein-design methods, with Marc Tessier-Lavigne as CEO. It is a pre-revenue biotech building both models and a pipeline of designed medicines.

owkin.name: Owkin
owkin.blurb: Federated learning across hospitals; pathology diagnostics and biomarker discovery; K Navigator agent.
owkin.overview: Owkin applies federated learning across hospital data to discover biomarkers and develop diagnostics, and sells AI pathology tests and research partnerships to pharma. It launched the K Navigator research agent in 2025.

pathai.name: PathAI
pathai.blurb: Digital pathology platform (AISight) and algorithms for pharma trials and diagnostics.
pathai.overview: PathAI sells the AISight digital pathology platform and algorithms used in pharma clinical trials and diagnostic labs. Revenue comes from software subscriptions and services to drug developers.

chai.name: Chai Discovery
chai.blurb: Chai-1 and Chai-2 molecular structure and antibody design models; OpenAI and Thrive backed.
chai.overview: Chai Discovery builds molecular structure and antibody-design models (Chai-1, Chai-2) and partners with pharma on design programmes. It is backed by OpenAI and Thrive and competes with Isomorphic and Generate on the model layer of drug design.

apple.name: Apple
apple.blurb: Apple Intelligence on-device plus Private Cloud Compute; licenses ChatGPT and Gemini for Siri; designs its own silicon, fabbed at TSMC.
apple.overview: Apple sells hardware (iPhone, Mac, iPad, Watch) and high-margin services. Its AI strategy is on-device models plus Private Cloud Compute, with ChatGPT and Gemini licensed for Siri's harder queries. It designs its own chips, fabbed at TSMC, and has been slow to ship a competitive assistant, which is the main debate about its AI position.

perplexity.name: Perplexity
perplexity.blurb: AI answer engine and Comet browser; distribution deals with Samsung, Motorola, airlines; NVIDIA, SoftBank, Bezos investors.
perplexity.overview: Perplexity is an AI answer engine and the Comet browser, monetised through Pro subscriptions, enterprise seats and advertising. It gains distribution through deals with Samsung, Motorola and airlines, and is backed by NVIDIA, SoftBank and Jeff Bezos. It competes with Google and ChatGPT search.

midjourney.name: Midjourney
midjourney.blurb: Bootstrapped image and video generator with ~$500M revenue; licensed its models to Meta (2025).
midjourney.overview: Midjourney is a bootstrapped image and video generation service sold by subscription, with roughly $500M in annual revenue and no outside investors. It licensed its models to Meta in 2025 and competes with OpenAI, Black Forest Labs and Adobe.

elevenlabs.name: ElevenLabs
elevenlabs.blurb: Voice synthesis, dubbing and conversational voice agents; fastest-growing voice AI company.
elevenlabs.overview: ElevenLabs sells voice synthesis, dubbing and conversational voice agents to media companies, developers and enterprises, priced by usage and seats. It is the fastest-growing voice AI company and expanded into music and agent platforms.

characterai.name: Character.AI
characterai.blurb: Companion chatbots; founders returned to Google in a $2.7B licensing deal (2024); under scrutiny over teen safety.
characterai.overview: Character.AI runs a companion-chatbot app monetised through subscriptions. Its founders returned to Google in a $2.7B licensing deal in 2024, and the company faces lawsuits and regulatory scrutiny over teen safety, which shapes the consumer-companion category.

runway.name: Runway
runway.blurb: Gen-4 video models for film and advertising; Lionsgate and AMC deals; Google, NVIDIA, Salesforce investors.
runway.overview: Runway builds video generation models (Gen-4) for film, advertising and creators, sold through subscriptions and enterprise deals with studios such as Lionsgate and AMC. It is backed by Google, NVIDIA and Salesforce.

suno.name: Suno
suno.blurb: Music generation; settled with Warner and licensing with labels after 2024 lawsuits; $250M round led by Menlo (2025).
suno.overview: Suno generates full songs from text prompts, sold by subscription. It was sued by the major labels in 2024 and has since moved toward licensing deals, including a settlement with Warner. It raised $250M led by Menlo in 2025.

blackforest.name: Black Forest Labs
blackforest.blurb: FLUX image models (ex-Stable Diffusion team); powers Grok image generation and Meta features.
blackforest.overview: Black Forest Labs, founded by the team behind Stable Diffusion, builds the FLUX image models. It licenses them to xAI (Grok image generation) and Meta and sells API access, competing with Midjourney and OpenAI.

luma.name: Luma AI
luma.blurb: Dream Machine / Ray video models; $900M Series C led by Humain (Saudi) with a 2 GW compute plan.
luma.overview: Luma AI builds the Dream Machine and Ray video and world models, sold via subscription and API. Its $900M Series C led by Saudi Arabia's Humain came with plans for 2 GW of compute, making it one of the best-capitalised video labs.

pika.name: Pika
pika.blurb: Consumer video effects app; pivoted toward social video.
pika.overview: Pika makes a consumer app for AI video effects and short-form creation. It has pivoted toward social features and competes with Runway, Luma and ByteDance's tools.

bytedance.name: ByteDance
bytedance.blurb: Doubao is China's most-used assistant; Seedance / Seedream media models; largest buyer of AI compute in China; custom chips with Broadcom.
bytedance.overview: ByteDance owns TikTok and Douyin and is the largest buyer of AI compute in China. Its Doubao assistant is China's most-used, and its Seedance and Seedream media models power creative tools. It monetises through advertising and e-commerce and designs custom chips with Broadcom to reduce NVIDIA dependence.

softbank.name: SoftBank
softbank.blurb: Largest single AI investor: $30B+ into OpenAI, Stargate JV, Ampere acquisition, Arm ownership, stakes in Skild and Perplexity. Sold its NVIDIA stake in 2025 to fund it.
softbank.overview: SoftBank is the largest single investor in AI: over $30B into OpenAI, the Stargate datacenter joint venture, ownership of Arm, acquisition of Ampere, and stakes in Skild and Perplexity. It funds this with Arm shares, margin loans and asset sales including its NVIDIA stake. Its returns are concentrated in OpenAI's outcome.

mgx.name: MGX / Gulf sovereign capital
mgx.blurb: Abu Dhabi's AI fund (with G42 and Mubadala), plus Saudi PIF/Humain and QIA: anchor LPs in Stargate, OpenAI, xAI, Anthropic rounds and datacenter builds.
mgx.overview: MGX is Abu Dhabi's AI investment vehicle alongside G42 and Mubadala, and together with Saudi Arabia's PIF and Humain and Qatar's QIA forms the Gulf capital that anchors Stargate, OpenAI, xAI and Anthropic rounds and funds datacenter builds in the region. The model is sovereign wealth seeking both returns and local AI capacity.

thrive.name: Thrive Capital
thrive.blurb: Josh Kushner's firm; led OpenAI's 2024 round and backs Anthropic, Cursor, Databricks, Physical Intelligence, Isomorphic.
thrive.overview: Thrive Capital, led by Josh Kushner, is a New York firm that led OpenAI's 2024 round and holds large positions in Anthropic, Cursor, Databricks, Physical Intelligence and Isomorphic. It concentrates capital in a small number of category leaders.

a16z.name: Andreessen Horowitz
a16z.blurb: $7B+ AI fund; xAI, Mistral, ElevenLabs, Black Forest Labs, Decagon, Hippocratic, Databricks; policy-active on open source.
a16z.overview: Andreessen Horowitz is the largest venture firm by assets, with multi-billion AI funds. It backs xAI, Mistral, ElevenLabs, Black Forest Labs, Decagon, Hippocratic and Databricks, and is politically active on open-source and regulation.

sequoia.name: Sequoia Capital
sequoia.blurb: OpenAI, xAI, Harvey, Sierra, OpenEvidence, ElevenLabs, Glean; the classic firm most exposed to the application layer.
sequoia.overview: Sequoia Capital is the classic Silicon Valley firm with stakes in OpenAI, xAI, Harvey, Sierra, OpenEvidence, ElevenLabs and Glean. It is most exposed to the application layer and has argued publicly about whether AI revenue justifies capex.

lightspeed.name: Lightspeed Venture Partners
lightspeed.blurb: Anthropic (led Series F), Mistral, Databricks, Glean, Pika; raised $9B in 2025.
lightspeed.overview: Lightspeed Venture Partners led Anthropic's Series F and backs Mistral, Databricks, Glean and Pika. It raised $9B in 2025, giving it one of the largest pools for late-stage AI rounds.

generalcatalyst.name: General Catalyst
generalcatalyst.blurb: Anthropic, Mistral, Hippocratic, Abridge, Lovable; owns a health system (Summa) to deploy health AI.
generalcatalyst.overview: General Catalyst invests across Anthropic, Mistral, Hippocratic, Abridge and Lovable and unusually owns a health system (Summa Health) to deploy health AI directly. It raised one of the largest venture funds of 2024.

coatue.name: Coatue
coatue.blurb: Crossover investor in OpenAI, Anthropic, Databricks, CoreWeave, Lambda, Scale.
coatue.overview: Coatue is a crossover hedge fund and venture investor with positions in OpenAI, Anthropic, Databricks, CoreWeave, Lambda and Scale. It invests from both public and private vehicles and publishes influential AI market research.

foundersfund.name: Founders Fund
foundersfund.blurb: Peter Thiel's firm: OpenAI, Anthropic, Scale, Cognition, Anduril, Crusoe.
foundersfund.overview: Founders Fund, Peter Thiel's firm, backs OpenAI, Anthropic, Scale, Cognition, Anduril and Crusoe. It is known for concentrated bets and defence-adjacent companies.

dragoneer.name: Dragoneer
dragoneer.blurb: Growth investor in OpenAI, Anthropic, Databricks, Cursor; led large 2025 secondaries.
dragoneer.overview: Dragoneer is a growth investor that led or joined large late-stage rounds and secondaries in OpenAI, Anthropic, Databricks and Cursor, often providing liquidity to employees.

greenoaks.name: Greenoaks
greenoaks.blurb: Concentrated bets: Sierra, Databricks, Anthropic, Scale, Figure.
greenoaks.overview: Greenoaks runs a concentrated portfolio with large positions in Sierra, Databricks, Anthropic, Scale and Figure, backing a handful of companies per year with significant cheques.

khosla.name: Khosla Ventures
khosla.blurb: First VC into OpenAI (2019); Replit, Glean, Commonwealth Fusion, Hermeus.
khosla.overview: Khosla Ventures was the first venture firm to invest in OpenAI in 2019 and backs Replit, Glean and deep-tech bets such as Commonwealth Fusion. Vinod Khosla is a vocal advocate for aggressive AI investment.

ycombinator.name: Y Combinator
ycombinator.blurb: Batches are now ~80% AI; the seed pipeline for agents, dev tools and vertical AI.
ycombinator.overview: Y Combinator is the leading startup accelerator, investing $500k in hundreds of companies per year; recent batches are around 80% AI companies, making it the seed pipeline for agents, developer tools and vertical AI.

index.name: Index Ventures
index.blurb: Scale AI, Cohere, Mistral, Harvey, Wayve, ElevenLabs.
index.overview: Index Ventures is a London and San Francisco firm with early stakes in Scale AI, Cohere, Mistral, Harvey, Wayve and ElevenLabs, giving it unusually strong exposure to European AI.

benchmark.name: Benchmark
benchmark.blurb: Small-fund model; Cerebras, Fireworks, Sierra, Manus (China-origin agent startup).
benchmark.overview: Benchmark keeps a small-fund, equal-partner model and backs Cerebras, Fireworks, Sierra and Manus. It is selective and does not raise growth funds, so its AI exposure is early-stage.
